text:
nora: quick results from our Lucid-13B quant sweep + GTN slice — need a short recommendation for product.
diego: short bullets pls.
nora: baseline FP16 (int8 in our infra) = p95 ~130ms, throughput ~900 tok/s, unit ~$0.047 / 1k. int6 variant = p95 ~145ms, throughput ~1.05k tok/s, unit ~$0.031 / 1k, QA delta ~0.6% abs on GTN dev mix. int4 = p95 ~180ms, throughput ~1.25k tok/s, unit ~$0.020 / 1k, QA delta ~2.8% abs; p99 spikes on >1k contexts.
aya: what about cold cache behavior?
nora: KV warmup matters: int6 matches int8 after warm; int4 has cold-cache instability and higher variance under burst.
sam: ops rec: route short conversational traffic (<=512 tokens) to int6 as pilot; keep int8 for longform/high-precision. start canary at 10%-20% with 7-day window. rollback triggers: QA delta >1.2% abs or p95 >250ms.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary started lucid-13b-int6 -> 15% traffic at 2024-09-03T11:00Z (simulated).
diego: batching note: microbench used batch=8. adaptive batching to max 12 saves ~8-10% cost but adds ~20ms p95. recommend adaptive with latency caps.
nora: unit-econ for slides: per-1M tokens cost: int8 ~$47k, int6 ~$31k (save ~$16k per 1M). pilot (15% of current traffic) estimated ~$2.7k/month savings; caveats: depends on batching and traffic shape.
aya: add regression tests: priming stability, long-context p99, factual-hallucination rate.
sam: product-friendly one-liner: "Run 7d pilot: 15% short-conversation traffic -> lucid-13b-int6; preserve int8 for longform; do not use int4 yet; enable adaptive batching with latency caps; automatic fallback on QA/latency breaches."
nora: I'll put together a micro-scorecard and dashboards and share by EOD.
diego: :thumbsup:
